source_text: Merito itaque non placet illi hypocrisis Pharisaeorum, labiis scilicet amantium deum, non corde. cauete, inquit discipulis, a fermento Pharisaeorum, quod est hypocrisis, non praedicatio creatoris. odit contumaces patris filius, non uult suos tales existere in illum, — non in alium — in quem hypocrisis fuit et admissa, cuius exemplum a discipulis caueretur. ita Pharisaeorum (cum) prohibet exemplum, in eum prohibebat illud admitti, in quem admittebant Pharisaei. igitur , quoniam hypocrisin eorum taxarat, utique celantem occulta cordis et incredulitatis secreta superficialibus officiis obumbrantem, quae clauem agnitionis habens nec [in] ipsa introiret nec alios sineret, ideo adicit: nihil autem opertum, quod non patefiet, et nihil absconditum, quod non dinoscetur, ne quis existimet illum dei ignoti retro et occulti reuelationem et adagnitionem intentare, cum subiciat etiam, quae intra se mussitarent uel inter se tractarent — scilicet super ipso diceutes: hic non expellit daemonia nisi in Belzebule — in apertum processura et in ore hominum futura, ex euangelii promulgatione.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore it is not pleasing to Him, the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, namely with lips loving God, not with the heart. Beware, He says to the disciples, of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy, not the preaching of the Creator. The Son of the Father hates the stubborn, does not want His own to be such in Him, — not in another — in whom hypocrisy was and was admitted, whose example was to be avoided by the disciples. Thus, while He prohibits the example of the Pharisees, He prohibits that it be admitted in Him, in whom the Pharisees admitted it. Therefore, since He censured their hypocrisy, surely hiding the secret things of the heart and the secrets of unbelief with superficial duties, which having the key of knowledge neither enters itself nor allows others to enter, therefore He adds: nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and nothing is hidden that will not be known, lest anyone think that He intends the revelation and recognition of the unknown God, backwards and hidden, since He also subjects to scrutiny even those things that they muttered among themselves or discussed — namely, speaking about Him: this one does not cast out demons except in Beelzebub — which will come to light and will be in the mouth of men, from the promulgation of the Gospel.

pass_b_english: No wonder He takes no pleasure in the hypocrisy of the Pharisees — people who honor God with their lips while their hearts are far from Him. "Watch out for the leaven of the Pharisees," He tells His disciples, "which is hypocrisy," not the preaching of the Creator (Matt. 16:6). The Son hates the stubborn; He refuses to let His own become like that toward Him — not toward someone else — toward the very One in whom hypocrisy took root and was tolerated, the One whose example the disciples were warned to avoid. So, when He forbids the Pharisees' example, He is forbidding that same corruption from taking hold in Him, the very One in whom the Pharisees indulged it. Because He has condemned their hypocrisy — a mask that hides the heart's secrets and unbelief behind superficial duties, a mask that holds the key of knowledge yet neither enters itself nor lets others in — He adds: "Nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and nothing hidden that will not be known" (Matt. 10:26). He says this so no one imagines He is staging some backward, covert revelation of an unknown God. After all, He drags into the open even the things they muttered among themselves or debated in private — specifically, their talk about Him: "He casts out demons only by Beelzebul" (Matt. 12:24) — words destined to become public knowledge and on everyone's lips through the proclamation of the Gospel.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent English version that preserves all nuances, including the complex distinction regarding hypocrisy being admitted 'in Him' (the Son) versus 'in another'. Scripture citations (Matt. 16:6, Matt. 10:26, Matt. 12:24) are correctly identified and correspond to the quoted/alluded content.
